  "rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.",
  "text": "It struck the gunwale without breaking.

The sound was small, almost courteous. Across the river, the open door slammed shut.

Elias remained outside.

The ferryman made a noise through his teeth and bent, but his fingers stopped above the brass frame. Blood from Mara’s knuckles ran along its edge.

“Pick it up.”

She stepped back.

On the opposite bank, Elias looked toward the closed door. For the first time, he seemed afraid of something other than the cold.

“What happens now?” she asked.

“The wrong person is outside.”

The mirror lay faceup between them. There was no desk in it now, only a ceiling crossed by dark beams. Mara knew those beams. Elias had cut his initials into one while she held the ladder and complained about the shavings in their bed.

Something scraped across the glass from underneath.

A chair being moved.

“You said it was tomorrow.”

“You asked if it was.”

Across the water, Elias started down the bank. His bad ankle folded beneath him. He caught himself on one knee, exactly as her brother would have done, and that was worse than the answers.

Mara crouched beside the mirror.

The older hand appeared against the glass, its scar matching the fresh cut on her own. One finger dragged slowly through the blood along the frame.

Not letters. A line, drawn across the brass.

A crossing-out.

Mara took the ferryman’s oar.

“No,” he said, with sudden relief, as though he had been waiting years to be allowed to protest.

She drove its iron tip into the glass.

Beneath her feet, someone knocked."
